Aisha (eng-arch): Quick sketch: instead of evaluating expressive policies in runtime we emit compact, verifiable decision blobs from a compiler. Runtime only runs an eval of that blob + tiny per-tenant delta. Thoughts?
Marco (eng-compiler): I like the isolation. Compiler can do heavy analysis (cost simulations, fallback graphs). We'll need a stable blob schema. Do we want human-readable (yaml/json) or compact binary?
Ethan (eng-runtime): Compact binary for perf. parsing per-request must be <1us ideally. maybe CBOR or flatbuffers. protobuf is fine if we keep lightweight.
Priya (eng-sre): Operationally, watching blobs, revoking, and hot rollback are big concerns. We need signed blobs + a revocation list. Also want canary percentage routing for new blobs.
Marco (eng-compiler): Agreed. Proposal: blob contains metadata: schema_version, semantic_hash (of policy source), tests_run_id, author, produced_at. Body: ordered candidates + constraints + explicit fallback edges. No code.
Aisha (eng-arch): Important: make fallback edges explicit to avoid runtime cycles. Compiler will validate DAG-ness and fallback coverage (every path must reach a safe default).
Ethan (eng-runtime): If runtime gets a malformed or incompatible blob, it should fall back to a well-known default route (safe_default) and emit a high-priority alert. No request should error because of policy parsing.
Priya (eng-sre): Auto-alert threshold: if >0.05% requests use safe_default for a given host in 5m window, page on-call.
Marco (eng-compiler): For per-tenant customizations, compiler emits a base blob and an optional per-tenant delta blob that only contains small overrides (score deltas, allow/deny flags). Delta blobs are explicitly bounded in size and apply at runtime after base selection.
Ethan (eng-runtime): Delta merging must be constant-time. Limit to "delta list" of (candidate_id, score_delta, TTL). No branching logic.
Aisha (eng-arch): On dynamic signals (region congestion/overload) we can push ephemeral override blobs with short TTL from control plane; they are signed and treated like deltas. Runtime enforces max TTL (e.g., 60s).
Marco (eng-compiler): Testing checklist for compiler: 1) DAG fallback validation 2) simulated traffic run to ensure at least X% of cases have a compatible candidate 3) regression tests for cost/latency targets. Store results in blob metadata.
Priya (eng-sre): Where are blobs stored? S3 with version metadata + signed manifest. Control plane exposes a watch endpoint for runtime to subscribe to blob updates per-region.
Ethan (eng-runtime): Implementation notes: runtime keeps an in-memory LRU cache of active blobs keyed by (tenant_id, blob_version). Blob load happens async on first request with fallback to previous blob. Hot-swap must be atomic.
Marco (eng-compiler): Schema sketch (pseudo):
```
blob: {
  version: 1,
  hash: "sha256:...",
  produced_by: "policy-compiler/3.2",
  tests: { sim_id: 123, coverage_pct: 98 },
  candidates: [
    { id: "gpu-pool-a", constraints: { region: "us-east-1", max_latency_ms: 120 }, score: 100 },
    { id: "cpu-quant", constraints: { quantized: true }, score: 60 }
  ],
  fallbacks: [ { from: "gpu-pool-a", to: "cpu-quant", reason: "latency_violation" } ],
  safe_default: "cpu-std",
  signature: "..."
}
```
Marco (eng-compiler): We'll compress & sign that.
Aisha (eng-arch): Perf target: end-to-end decision overhead <= 0.5ms median, p99 under 2ms for small blobs. That includes parsing/merge and simple constraint checks.
Ethan (eng-runtime): We'll bench with flatbuffers and protobuf. Flatbuffers avoids allocations but protobuf might be easier for iteration. I'll prototype both.
Priya (eng-sre): Security: require KMS-backed signatures and include a short TTL on signed tokens for delta blobs. Add audit logs for each blob activation.
Aisha (eng-arch): Observability: emitted events should include chosen_candidate, list of considered candidates (ids only), rejection_reasons (enum), blob_version, and optional sim_coverage. That ties compiler feedback loop to real traffic.
Marco (eng-compiler): One subtlety: prefer deterministic tie-breakers. Blob should encode deterministic ordering when scores tie (e.g., lexicographic id or explicit priority).
Ethan (eng-runtime): Good point. Also need to handle partial candidate compatibility: candidate may be region-compatible but exceed token_budget — runtime should support evaluating numeric constraints quickly.
Aisha (eng-arch): Action plan: Marco -> write blob schema doc + compiler validations; Ethan -> prototype parser + perf numbers; Priya -> runbook for blob revocation + alert thresholds; I'll draft a short RFC describing control-plane lifecycle + security model.
Priya (eng-sre): Ops automation: ops-bot, once RFC is posted, please create a checklist for canary monitoring (error rates, safe_default usage, latency regressions).
ops-bot: will do. creating a template for canary monitors and automated rollback triggers. :robot_face:
Ethan (eng-runtime): I'll target a PoC in staging that only covers cost-tiering and safe_default behavior. Can we limit scope to one region for PoC?
Aisha (eng-arch): Yes, start with us-east-1 and tenant-sample. Keep rollout to 1% traffic initially.
Marco (eng-compiler): I'll also include a small fuzzer that randomly generates fallback graphs to stress the DAG validator.
Aisha (eng-arch): Thanks team. RFC expected by EOD +1. Short follow-up next week after PoC metrics. :thumbsup:
